Current claim and scaffold route retained: Let $\lambda\vdash n$ be a partition with English Young diagram $[\lambda]$ ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]) and let $\nu\subseteq\lambda$ be a subpartition, so that the skew diagram $[\lambda/\nu]$ is the set of nodes of $[\lambda]$ outside $[\nu]$ ([[def-skew-diagram-and-semistandard-skew-tableau]]).

A **removable border strip** of $\lambda$ (also called a **skew hook** or **rim hook**) is a nonempty set $\xi$ of nodes of $[\lambda]$ such that (i) $\xi$ is edge-connected (any two nodes of $\xi$ are joined by a chain of side-adjacent nodes of $\xi$), (ii) $\xi$ contains no $2\times2$ block of nodes, and (iii) $[\lambda]\setminus\xi$ is again the Young diagram of a partition $\nu$. Equivalently, a removable border strip is a skew diagram $\lambda/\nu$ that is connected and contains no $2\times2$ block, i.e. a connected part of the rim of $[\lambda]$ whose removal leaves a Young diagram; we then write $\xi=\lambda/\nu$.

The **size** of $\xi$ is its number of nodes; a removable border strip of size $r$ is a **removable $r$-strip**, and then $\nu\vdash n-r$. The **height** (also **leg length**) of a nonempty connected border strip $\xi$ is
$$
\operatorname{ht}(\xi):=(\text{number of distinct rows of }[\lambda]\text{ occupied by }\xi)-1.
$$
If such a strip has $r$ nodes and occupies $c$ columns and $w$ rows, then $w=r-c+1$, hence $\operatorname{ht}(\xi)=r-c\ge0$; in particular $\operatorname{ht}(\xi)=0$ for a horizontal strip and $c=r-\operatorname{ht}(\xi)$. A removable border strip of size $1$ is exactly a removable node ([[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]]). No choice principle is used.
